results.fact: Car-to-car total time vs its own schedule
results.evidence: Still unsettled. The schedule (3:30 AM start, back 5-6 PM) implies 13.5-14.5 h against totalHrs / day hours of 11 and the 10-12 h note. New reports cover mostly the East Ridge (about 14 h car-to-car on one outing, a little under 9.5 h on another), and a club route profile splits the West Ridge into trailhead-to-camp 4 h, camp-to-summit 6 h and summit-to-trailhead 4-6 h as a two-day trip while noting many parties do it in one long day. Reported one-day West Ridge times still range from about 10.5 h to over 14 h, so no single figure is supported by two sources.

results.fact: Total time vs its own sub-components
results.evidence: Unchanged in the live row: timing shows approach 5, summit 6, descent 6, total 13 (the col-to-col climbing day), so the parts do not sum to the total. Resolving it needs a decision on whether PUBLISHED TIMES describes the climbing day (drop the approach, total 12) or the whole trip (which would also need a hike-out figure no source pins down); reports vary too widely to supply a researched car-to-car total, and the total cannot be computed by adding legs.

results.fact: Whether the route involves glacier travel / needs a rope and crevasse-rescue gear
results.evidence: Retry found only the same class of evidence: the Buckindy High Route report (the ice now survives only on the highest north-facing slopes and the ascent via the remnant glacier was straightforward) and Snowking/Kindy Ridge pages that describe the approach but not Mutchler's standard line. No second independent source says whether the Kindy Ridge / Cyclone Lake line to Mutchler needs roped glacier travel, so detailed_rack/pro_needs (glacier kit) and seasonal_hazards.crevasses ('no glacier travel') stay as they are.

Still unsettled: dist_km 24.78 renders as the one-way approach while the approach prose calls ~24.8 km the round trip and 12-14 km the one-way figure; waypoints put the summit 7.7 mi out and the itinerary sums 17.5 mi. Sources found give figures for Snowking (not Mutchler) via Kindy Ridge, and no source states a one-way car-to-Mutchler distance; halving a round trip is not allowed.

results.fact: Elevation of the Standup Creek Trail junction waypoint
results.evidence: The ground elevation at the junction's stored pin is about 5,330 ft (USGS point query), but the pin itself sits beside the upper-meadow camp pin rather than 0.3 mi past the creek crossing (whose own pin reads about 4,360 ft on the ground against a stored 4,800), so the pin cannot be trusted as the junction's location. Trail sources place the junction about 2 mi below Navaho Pass but give no elevation for it; with no source for the junction's height the stored 5,450 is left unchanged.

results.fact: Crux/route grade (Class 4, 5.0) vs. the pitch-by-pitch breakdown's max grade (Class 3)
results.evidence: Still unsettled. The only detailed account of the Needle Peak north ridge describes exposed cliff bands at 7,300-7,400 ft and a tree belay at a slick 5,000 ft slab gully without naming a class; a route page for the neighbouring Swamp Creek line (Dark Peak) gives Class 3 with a Class 3/4 option, which is a different peak. No two sources grade this route's crux, so grade 'Class 4 (5.0 crux)' and the Class 3 pitch_detail maximum are left as they are.

results.fact: Whether a permit office exists at Stehekin
results.evidence: The park's own permits page states that no permit services are available in Stehekin (walk-up requests are made by email the day before travel), agreeing with a current permit guide; a local article adds that self-issue at the Stehekin ranger station applies only when the Marblemount center is closed for winter. The row matches all of this: overnight_permit and the bivy notes say there is no permit office in Stehekin, access.permit limits Stehekin self-issue to when the information center is unstaffed, and the emergency field names the Stehekin visitor center only as a contact, not a permit office.

results.evidence: already consistent. partner_requirements now places the crux in the exposed cliff bands at 7,300-7,400 ft 'well below the broad summit', and seasonal_hazards.exposure names the cliff bands and the notch above them; neither still mentions a narrow summit step.
